key_insight: A high-order FR/CPR solver coupled with a rotating actuator-line model can predict VAWT aerodynamics on fixed Cartesian grids without resolving blade geometry.
engineering_relevance: This geometry-free approach offers a computationally efficient way to study rotating-blade wakes and power performance, making it useful for large-scale wind-energy design and parametric sweeps.
method: FR/CPR flow solver on fixed Cartesian grids
Rotating actuator-line model with isotropic Gaussian force projection
Modified Boeing-Vertol dynamic stall model and DMST inflow correction
evidence_signal: The method was validated against experimental near-wake measurements and prior LES-ALM results, with power coefficients matching high-fidelity 3D LES-ALM data within 6% near optimal operating conditions.
watch_item: Accuracy depends on choosing a sufficiently resolved Gaussian projection kernel and may require DMST correction when coarse meshes reduce inflow/induction fidelity.
paper_title: A High-Order Flux Reconstruction Actuator-Line Framework for Rotating-Blade Aerodynamics on Fixed Cartesian Grids
